# How to Ask Alexa+ for Weather-Based Outfit Suggestions

> **In short:** Alexa+ can combine today's forecast with your plans and saved preferences to suggest an outfit in one conversation. The trick is asking for weather *and* clothing in the same sentence, and saving your preferences so you don't have to repeat them every morning.

You already know how to talk to Alexa+. This guide adds one morning routine that pays back every day: asking for clothing ideas that actually match the weather, your schedule, and your style — without opening a forecast app, a calendar, or your closet, all at the same time.

## Before you start
- An **Alexa+ enabled** Echo device, or the Alexa+ app on your phone. Amazon says Alexa+ is rolling out gradually, so confirm your device shows the Alexa+ experience.
- An account that has access to Alexa+ (Amazon says it is bundled with Prime in some regions — check the current plan details on Amazon's official Alexa+ page if you're unsure).
- About **3 minutes** the first time, under a minute on regular mornings once your preferences are saved.

## Step 1 — Ask for weather and outfit in one sentence
Wake Alexa+ with your usual wake word, then ask **one question that covers both the data and the intent**. A simple "Alexa, what's the weather?" gets you a forecast — but if you also ask what to wear, Alexa+ treats it as a single task and answers both. Speak the way you would to a friend, then pause for the response. On an Echo with a screen, you'll see the forecast card appear while Alexa+ speaks; on a speaker-only Echo, you'll just hear the answer. If your device uses a custom wake word, say that instead.
💬 Example: "Alexa, what's the forecast for today, and what should I wear?"
You'll know it worked when Alexa+ answers with both the day's weather **and** at least one concrete clothing suggestion — not just a temperature reading.

## Step 2 — Add context about your day and your style
The first answer is usually generic. Strengthen it by mentioning where you're going, how active you'll be, and any dress code you follow. Alexa+ uses these details to narrow the suggestion — a 9-to-5 office day calls for different clothing than a park walk with the kids. Be specific but casual; you don't need a formal prompt, just real-life details. If Alexa+ doesn't pick up on a detail you gave, restate it more directly ("I mean I sit at a desk most of the day").
💬 Example: "I have meetings until 3 p.m., then I'm picking up the kids. I'm usually in business casual."
You'll know it worked when the next suggestion clearly reflects your situation — something like "wear layers, keep a blazer handy" — instead of a generic coat-and-boots answer.

## Step 3 — Ask for a backup plan for weather changes
Weather rarely stays put. Ask Alexa+ to plan for the worst case so you're not caught out by an unexpected cold snap, a sudden shower, or a temperature drop after sunset. This is the kind of multi-step, contingent question Alexa+ handles better than older versions of Alexa — older Alexa typically answered the literal question only. If your device doesn't seem to handle the contingency, try breaking it into two shorter asks.
💬 Example: "What if it gets colder in the evening, or if it rains on my way home?"
You'll know it worked when you get a **layered or contingency** suggestion — a cardigan to pack, a foldable umbrella, waterproof shoes — instead of just one fixed outfit.

## Step 4 — Tell Alexa+ to remember your preferences for next time
This is where the workflow gets genuinely useful. Ask Alexa+ to save the preferences you just described — fit, colors you avoid, what counts as "too cold" for you — so future mornings don't require you to repeat them. Amazon says Alexa+ has a memory feature that stores these for later conversations. If the in-conversation "remember" doesn't seem to stick on your device, the same preferences can also be set in the Alexa app under a section like **Settings → Alexa Preferences → Voice Responses** (the exact label varies by app version). The in-conversation route is faster when it works.
💬 Example: "Remember that I prefer layers, avoid bright colors, and run cold at anything under 60°F."
You'll know it worked when Alexa+ **confirms the memory out loud** ("Got it, I'll remember that"), or when your next outfit question already reflects the preferences without you repeating them.

## Step 5 — Make it part of your morning with a Routine
The biggest time-saver: turn this into an automatic briefing so you never have to ask. In the Alexa app, open **Routines** (look for a "Your Routines" or "Routines" section in the menu) and create a new one. Set a time trigger for when you usually get ready — pick a time you'll reliably be near the device, not a "should be awake" time you never hit. Add a custom action that runs your outfit-and-weather request, with the preferences from Step 4 baked in. Some Alexa+ capabilities may only be available on certain plans — if a Routine step won't go through, check the current Alexa+ plan details on Amazon's official page.
💬 Example: Time trigger 7:15 a.m. → Custom action: "Give me today's forecast, my saved outfit preferences, and what I should wear today."
You'll know it worked when, at the chosen time, your Echo lights up **on its own** and delivers a weather-plus-outfit briefing without you saying a word.

## Common mistakes
- **Asking only one half of the question.** "What's the weather?" gets a forecast, not clothing ideas. Combine both in one sentence so Alexa+ treats it as a single task.
- **Skipping the "remember this" step.** Without it, you'll repeat your preferences every morning — fine once, tiring by Wednesday. Save them once, reuse them all week.
- **Setting the Routine trigger too early.** If Alexa+ starts briefing you before you're actually awake, you'll mute or skip the Routine within a week. Pick a realistic time you reliably have the device nearby.

## What this means for you
- **In everyday life:** A small morning ritual that gives you one less decision before coffee, and one less app to open before the door.
- **For your work or business:** If your work involves showing up somewhere — clients, school, events — a weather-aware suggestion cuts down on those days you walk out underdressed or overdressed.
- **If you want to go further:** Layer in your calendar. Try asking Alexa+ to factor in your first meeting of the day, so a 10 a.m. site visit pulls more practical suggestions than an 11 a.m. desk session. Once that works, save it as part of the same Routine.

## Try it now
Say it once, right now, while you're thinking about it: **"Alexa, what's the forecast for today, and what should I wear?"** Then refine the answer with one real detail from your day tomorrow. Two minutes today, and Wednesday morning is already half-handled.
